newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 19.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 19.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the
Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - International Business Machines Corp is set to launch a $90 million advertising campaign for its latest AS/400 computer line with in-flight commercials, magazine ads and banners on the World Wide Web starting this week, the Wall Street Journal reports.
NEW YORK - Sprint Corp, the nation's third-largest long-distance phone company, says it will be the sole sponsor of the North American part of the Rolling Stones' upcoming concert tour.

LONDON - Internet advertising is expected to grow rapidly over the next five years as advertisers take advantage of more sophisticated measurement methods to target specific users, says a report published by Zenith Media, the UK media planning and buying unit of Cordiant Plc.
ZURICH - Advertising pages in Swiss newspapers rose 1.0 percent in July compared with a year earlier, according to figures compiled by the WEMF media
tracking agency.

PHOENIX - Outdoor Systems Inc completes its $1.0 billion acquisition of Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Co's outdoor advertising unit, National Advertising Co. It says it now reaches 75 percent of the U.S. population with roughly 220,000 poster, bulletin, bus shelter, subway and mall displays in 46
states.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MADRID - Spain's Antena 3 television station appoints Telefonica secretary general Jose Mas Millet as its new chairman, effectively assuming control of the private television channel in defiance of the European Commission. The EC last week warned the telecoms operator to get EU approval before going ahead with its purchase of Antena 3.
LONDON - Two of Britain's leading booksellers, Dillons and Blackwells, are launching Internet bookstores, jumping on the growing bandwagon of
bookchains seeking wider sales via the Web.

LONDON - Europe's biggest telecommunications companies are racing to increase their Internet access business, while at the same time competing with the Internet by expanding their own online services, says Datamonitor, a
research consultancy.
PARIS - Amaury, the French press group which owns sports daily L'Equipe and popular daily Le Parisien, is working on launching a television sports news channel, financial daily Les Echos says.

NEW YORK - McGraw-Hill Cos Inc President Harold McGraw III says he does not expect the company to buy more television stations, and he would consider swapping its four stations for a publishing or information business.

TOKYO - Asian telecom operators including NTT and Telekom Malaysia Bhd will take stakes in Japanese Internet access provider Asia Internet Holding as it upgrades its Asian networks later this year. Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp is expected to take about a 15 percent stake in the Internet access provider for about 240 million yen ($2 million).
CHICAGO - Sex is the most searched-for topic on the Internet and the quest for it is driving the net's technological advances and spurring the next sexual revolution, say researchers.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - China became the world's leading market for frozen foods in 1996, accounting for consumption of 3.8 million tonnes and overtaking the U.S. as rising disposable income and an increasing taste for Western convenience foods propelled growth, a market research group reports.
DETROIT - Ford Motor Co confirms it will introduce a new sporty luxury sedan, smaller than its current offerings and called the LS6 and LS8, in the first part of 1999.

DARIEN, Connecticut - Labatt Brewing Co Ltd agrees with Lowenbrau AG of Germany to make Lowenbrau beers in North America. Sales of Lowenbrau in the U.S. have declined from around 1.2 million barrels annually in 1980 to about 400,000 barrels currently.

NEW DELHI - India's Him Neel Breweries Ltd and Germany's Haake-Beck Brauerie AG have set up a 550 million rupee ($15.4 million) brewery in northern India, the United News of India says. The beer will be marketed under the Haake-Beck brand name and will be available in India from next month.

COLOMBO - Sri Lanka's Ceylon Cold Stores Ltd is beating multinationals on its home patch because the company's century-old name inspires brand loyalty and its green Elephant trademark is a byword, according to analysts. The company has about 42 percent of the soft drinks market and its net profits grew by 73 percent to 152.78 million rupees ($2.6 million) in the financial
year to March 31, 1997.

LONDON - Britain's Jaguar Cars Ltd confirms it has launched a study into a new, smaller car which would double its annual output, although it is unlikely that the car -- called the X400 -- would ever be built in Britain.

WASHINGTON - Sri Lanka's tea industry is primed to regain its former dominance in the global black tea market, the World Bank says in a report. Sri Lanka's tea production is benefiting from the deregulation and privatization of its publicly owned plantation companies, says the bank.
UNIVERSAL CITY, California - Sega Gameworks raises $76 million for its expanding chain of interactive entertainment venues and says it will use the capital to open new GameWorks.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
TEL AVIV - A new Internet site that mimics the layout of a theme park is

launched in the U.S. The Virtual Community of Tomorrow, developed by Israel-based Community Network Systems, comprises 20 "pavilions" offering everything from Reuters news to on-line art exhibits, medical information and games.

BEIJING - Chinese people are forking out an arm and a leg for bone-stretching surgery. Dr Xia Hetao of the Institute of External Skeleton Fixation Technology in Beijing is just one surgeon who, for around 20-30,000 yuan ($3,610), will stretch the patient's bones with a steel frame. Many customers believe a boost in physical stature will also boost their social standing.
